newsitem.title: PERU: LIMA SHARES END WITH SLIGHT GAIN ON THIN TRADE.
newsitem.headline: LIMA SHARES END WITH SLIGHT GAIN ON THIN TRADE.

text.p: Lima shares closed up slightly Wednesday in thin trade, as foreign investors remained in the more profitable Mexican market and local investors diversified by buying stocks with good prospects, brokers said.
The majority of leaders recorded a rise in prices.
The brokers added that the same tendencies should be expected for Thursday.
Wednesday, the General Index rose 0.85 percent to 2038.12 points as the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 0.88 percent to 2929.59 points.
In 1,621 transactions, volume was 33 million soles ($12.5 million).

"The majority of local investors are buying good shares with attractive prices," said Edgar Saravia from local Latinoamericana brokerage. "Investors hope sectors like construction, which increased a lot during the first half, will maintain the same tendencies."
The construction sector recorded a 16.8 percent year-over- year increase during the first half.
Percy Romero, of local Fortuna brokerage, added the recovery of zinc prices had benefited the mining companies.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru remained stable at 6.24 soles on volume of 1.3 million shares.

The biggest winners among leaders were miner Volcan, which rose 9.53 percent to 23.45 soles on volume of 731,000 shares; miner Perubar, which went up 3.17 percent to 8.45 soles on volume of 85,832 shares; and miner Buenaventura, which climbed 2.97 percent to 22.50 soles on volume of 42,861 shares traded.
Cement producer Cementos Lima also rose 1.82 percent to 5.60 soles on volume of 119,000 shares.

There were only four losers among leaders. They were electricity producer Edegel, which fell 2.83 percent to 1.03 soles on volume of 474,000 shares, and electricity distributor Edelnor, which dropped 0.6 percent to 1.66 soles on volume of 22,181 shares.
"Investors are selling electric company stocks because of very low profitability," said Romero.

The other two losers were candy producer D'Onofrio, which fell 1.9 percent to 1.03 soles on volume of 50,129 shares and food company Alicorp which fell 0.81 percent to 3.66 soles on volume of 58,020 shares traded.
